description:
FILED s473t6a (Opus, 2026-09-16) by #1501 ROUND 8 (t6a), CHECK 2 of
t/op/filetest.t.  PRE-EXISTING.  47 blessed rows, the file's largest cluster.

perl lets a class overload the FILETEST operators with the `-X` key: the
handler is called as `$handler->($obj, $op_letter, '')` and its value IS the
filetest's value.  PCL already dispatches the PLAIN spelling (s470bs).  What it
does not do is dispatch under STACKING.

PROBED, scratch/s473t6a/probes/ft-overload.pl, perl 5.40.3 vs PCL 2ac855aa:

  package OverFtest;
  use overload fallback => 1, '-X' => sub { "-$_[1]" };
  sub new { bless {}, shift }
  package main;
  my $ft = OverFtest->new;
  print -r $ft;        # perl -r    PCL -r      (the plain spelling works)
  print -r -f $ft;     # perl -r    PCL undef
  print -f -r $ft;     # perl -f    PCL undef

perl answers the OUTERMOST (leftmost) operator's handler call; PCL answers
undef, because the s417 stacking lowering rewrites `-r -f $x` into perl's
`_`-chain (`-f $x && -r _`) and the `_` half never sees the object.

ROWS (baselines/perl-suite-fails.tsv, all now carrying this task):
  44 = `stacked overloaded -X` + `overloaded stacked -X`, two per letter for
       r w x o R W X O e z s f d l p S b c t u g k T M A B C (t/op/filetest.t
       lines 253-254, `is( eval "-r -$op \$ft", "-r", ... )`).
   3 = `string overload is called for -t on IO` and the same for -T and -B.
       The file's own comment says "IO refs always get string overload called.
       This might be a bug." -- perl calls the `""` handler for exactly those
       three operators on an IO ref; PCL does not ($over stays 0).

FIX SHAPE: the `_`-chain desugaring (docs/b1-operand-grammar-s416.md, #372) is
right for a plain operand and wrong for an OVERLOADED one, because perl's
stack collapses to ONE handler call there.  So the runtime filetest entry has
to ask `p-find-overload ... "-X"` BEFORE it consults the stat buffer, and the
STACK has to reach it -- which means the emission must carry the whole stack
(the letters, in order) rather than a pre-expanded `&&` chain, or the first
`-X` in the chain must take the object and the rest must be suppressed.  PROBE
THE BREAKING CASE: `-e -f "/etc/passwd"` is 1 in perl and undef when nested
(the s417 finding), so whatever replaces the chain must keep that.
subject: A -X OVERLOAD is not consulted under STACKING: -r -f $obj answers undef where perl calls the class's handler for the OUTERMOST op -- 47 rows in t/op/filetest.t
